concept.feedback: The proposal cleanly satisfies all listed gates. Its target remains exactly the locally defined checksum-selected participant, without imposing an external role or additional success condition.

findings.detail: The conservation-workshop artifact trail, handling records, access logs, tool records, and environmental readings fit workshop provenance naturally.
The premise states the locally defined ledger mechanism and identifies the checksum criterion as the complete success condition.
Tracing a damaged ceremonial object through intake, imaging, treatment, stabilization, and quarantine is a coherent workshop-review scenario.
No participant name, role, seniority, appearance order, or ordinary custody inference is presented as a shortcut to the target.
The proposal explicitly requires relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses to be combined in order under the local iterated modular checksum.
The premise centers on provenance review and evidence-ledger evaluation across workshop rooms, rather than an enclosed-crime or locked-room setup.
findings.gate: low resemblance to a stock locked-room mystery

final.feedback: Accept. The item is self-contained, calculation-driven, and does not disclose the qualifying candidate in the reader-facing text.

findings.detail: The story supplies the status scale, six stream order, coefficients, starting and accepted tallies, all five participants' six status values, and an unambiguous iterative modulo procedure.
The conservation-workshop narrative coherently frames the distributed records and calculation, while the procedural details remain understandable.

Resolving the main question requires collecting one value from each of six evidence streams for each candidate and applying the stated multi-pass calculation; it cannot be answered from a single record entry.

The reader-facing story never states that Logan Kline, or any other named participant, satisfies the final tally condition. The answer-bearing gold and validation fields are outside the story and questions.

The main question requests a full name, the lookup question requests an exact status word, the counterfactual specifies its intervention and permitted fallback answer, and the scalar question requests an exact integer.

story.feedback: deterministic, grounding, and model story critics accept
